endpoints.note: tpm_min and monthly_calls_min are null where the limit does not apply (Consents, 5.1.1 and 5.2).

response_time.index: round(0.95 * n), nearest integer (half up), 1-based in the ascending order
response_time.reported_by: CLIENT; SERVER when the report is UNPAIRED

availability.reported_by: CLIENT; SERVER when the report is UNPAIRED
availability.daily: available / (available + unavailable); minutes without valid requests are undefined and left out
availability.long: mean of the daily values of the last 90 calendar days, undefined days left out
availability.month: every day at or above daily_min, and the long value of the last day at or above long_min

traffic_key: origin: the organizationId of the caller
limits.operational_counts: 2XX responses only; extra requests for pagination are not counted

pcm_reporting.process_timespan: whole milliseconds, rounded up (a report with 0 is left out of the response time)

consents-renewal-frequency.what: The manual (5) says the endpoints of the consent API must be considered alta (1500 ms); the portal's table lists extends and extensions as baixa (4000 ms).
consents-renewal-frequency.chosen: The portal's value: it is the one given per endpoint.

p95-boundary.what: The manual (5.3.2) says at most the SLA (<=); its example and the portal's daily rule say below it (<).

daily-availability-denominator.what: The manual's formula divides by available + unavailable minutes; the portal's steps define total_minutos as the minutes of the day.
daily-availability-denominator.chosen: The manual's formula; its worked example divides by 1390, not 1440.

availability-method.what: The portal page of 2024 measures by polling GET /discovery/status every 30 seconds, with 3 months; the manual measures real requests by minute, with 90 days.

process-timespan-end.what: The field's definition ends the time at the first byte of the response; its filling rule and the manual end it at the last byte.

client-408-counting.what: A PAIRED_INCONSISTENT report of a CLIENT with 408 counts as sent at 15000 ms or more in the rule and the example, and below 15000 ms in the note that follows.
client-408-counting.chosen: 15000 ms or more: the rule and the example agree, and it is the timeout.

overload-in-availability.what: 529 is in the 5XX range, so literally it is an error in availability, although it is left out of the response time.
overload-in-availability.chosen: The literal reading: 529 counts as an error in availability.

pcm-spec-domains.what: The PCM's OpenAPI file and the portal's pages give other domains: rejectedBy INICIADORA, USUARIO, DETENTORA (portal USER, ASPSP, TPP); the server's dropReason has 'NO_CREDENTIAL, NONE' as one value and no CREDENTIAL_UNAVAILABLE; authorisationFlowIntent CIBA_FLOW (portal CIBA); naturezaJurídica with an accent.
pcm-spec-domains.chosen: The portal's pages, which are newer than the file; the reports' schema errors on these values are expected (services/validator/tests/test_telemetry.py).

process-timespan-integer.what: processTimespan is whole milliseconds in its definition and a number with an example of 120.000001.
process-timespan-integer.chosen: Whole milliseconds, rounded up, so a fast call is not reported as 0 and left out.

response-time-day.what: The day's time zone is stated for availability (Brasília) and not for the response time.

tpm-window.what: The manual sets transactions per minute (5.1.1) without saying whether the minute is the calendar minute or any 60 seconds.
tpm-window.chosen: A 429 is early when the origin sent the endpoint fewer requests than the TPM in the 60 seconds before it, so a calendar or a sliding minute that allows the minimum passes. The transmitter counts calendar minutes.

pagination-requests.what: The extra requests of a pagination are not counted for the monthly limit (5.2), without saying which they are.
pagination-requests.chosen: The requests for page 2 onward; they are not refused with 423 either.
